page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, scoring 66660.83 in stress-ng multi-core tests, and strong memory read bandwidth, reaching 208.32 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Passmark database operations and extended instruction tests also rank in the strong tier. However, single-core execution and text processing benchmarks fall into the average category.

The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached EBS volumes, which is mitigated by the high-speed 100 Gbps network interface. Large-model LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the 7B model achieving only 7.23 tokens per second. This hardware profile is suited for network-bound compute workloads, distributed database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, and high-throughput web serving.
